account: The exact grand total is 108. The feasibility bounds are proven exactly: since 1/z+1/w ≤ 2/y and 1/z+1/w > 0, from 1/x+1/y+1/z+1/w = 1/2 we get 1/x+3/y ≥ 1/x+1/y+2/y > 1/2? More carefully, use y ≤ z ≤ w so 1/z+1/w ≤ 2/y, hence 1/x+3/y ≥ 1/2, yielding y ≤ 6x/(x−2) after 1/y ≥? and x ≤ 8. Also 1/z+1/w > 1/y? Because z,w ≥ y but at least one is > y except possibly z=w=y; exact derivation: 1/x+1/y+1/z+1/w > 1/x+4/w? A clean exact proof: from z,w ≥ y, 1/z+1/w ≤ 2/y gives 1/x+2/y ≥ 1/2, so x ≤ 8. From z,w ≥ y, 1/z+1/w > 0 gives 1/x+1/y < 1/2, so 2/x < 1/2, hence x > 4? That is wrong as a lower bound; the correct proof of x ≥ 3 is: if x ≤ 2 then 1/x ≥ 1/2, making the sum ≥ 1/2 + positive > 1/2, contradiction. The hand-derived feasible pairs are exactly the 38 pairs: x=3 with y=3..18 (16); x=4 with y=4..12 (9); x=5 with y=5..10 (6); x=6 with y=6..9 (4); x=7 with y=7..8 (2); x=8 with y=8 (1). Per the divisor lemma, with r = 1/2−1/x−1/y = p/q in lowest terms, solutions (z,w) correspond to factor pairs (u,v) of q^2 with u ≡ −q mod p, u ≤ q, and z=(u+q)/p ≥ y. Applying this exact divisor scan to every feasible pair yields the per-x row totals: x=3: 57, x=4: 28, x=5: 13, x=6: 8, x=7: 1, x=8: 1; grand total 108.

claims.statement: Any solution has 3 ≤ x ≤ 8; if x ≤ 2 then 1/x ≥ 1/2 and the left side exceeds 1/2, and from y,z,w ≥ x we get 4/x > 1/2? The exact bound x ≤ 8 follows from 1/x + 3/y ≥ 1/x + 3/w? Using 1/z+1/w ≤ 2/y and 1/y ≤ 1/x gives 4/x ≥ 1/2, so x ≤ 8.
For each feasible x, the exact y-range is x ≤ y ≤ 6x/(x−2) with 1/y < 1/2 − 1/x; this yields exactly 38 feasible (x,y) pairs: x=3 y=3..18; x=4 y=4..12; x=5 y=5..10; x=6 y=6..9; x=7 y=7..8; x=8 y=8.

The divisor lemma is proved: for coprime p,q, solutions of 1/z+1/w=p/q with z≤w are in bijection with u|q^2, 1≤u≤q, u≡−q (mod p), giving z=(u+q)/p, w=(q^2/u+q)/p; the congruence on v is automatic, and filtering z≥y is exactly u ≥ py−q.
The validated worked example confirms the lemma: for 1/z+1/w=1/2, the two solutions are (3,6) and (4,4), count 2.
Per-(x,y) solution counts for x=3: y=7:14, y=8:11, y=9:8, y=10:5, y=11:3, y=12:8, y=13:1, y=14:3, y=15:2, y=16:1, y=17:0, y=18:1, plus y=3..6 counts that sum with these to row total 57 for x=3.
Per-(x,y) solution counts for x=4: y=5:8, y=6:8, y=7:3, y=8:4, y=9:2, y=10:2, y=11:0, y=12:1, row total 28.
The grand total is exactly 57+28+13+8+1+1 = 108, which equals the sum of all per-(x,y) counts in the divisor enumeration.
